teile.name: Hook
teile.text: A billion was pledged. Only $133 million arrived. But that wasn't the strangest part.
teile.szene: A clear close-up illustration of a financial ledger showing columns of figures with a highlighted deficit, resting on a wooden desk under soft directional lighting, medium shot.

teile.name: Founding
teile.text: OpenAI began in December 2015 as a nonprofit, with Musk and Altman as co-chairs.
teile.szene: An illustrative depiction of two colleagues collaborating over notes in a modest startup office in 2015, medium shot, warm natural window lighting.

teile.name: Gap
teile.text: Tax filings through 2021 confirmed the shortfall. So who joined anyway, and why?
teile.szene: An illustrative shot of an open folder with fiscal reports and numerical charts on a dark tabletop, shallow depth of field, professional cool lighting.

teile.name: Hiring
teile.text: Greg Brockman met Yoshua Bengio, listed great AI researchers, and hired nine that December.
teile.szene: An illustrative group of professionals reviewing a document together in a modern meeting room, medium shot, clear daylight, collaborative atmosphere.

teile.name: Refused offers
teile.text: No stock options, lower pay. Zaremba refused offers worth two to three times his market value.
teile.szene: An illustrative close-up of a person reading an employment contract in an office, focused warm desk lighting, calm and deliberate gesture.

teile.name: Payoff
teile.text: That billion was mostly a promise. The mission was what researchers actually joined.
teile.szene: An illustrative depiction of early artificial intelligence researchers collaborating in a workspace with computers and whiteboards, medium shot, soft office lighting.

teile.name: Call to action
teile.text: Be sure to like, share and save this video.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game poster style: the blue-eyed fedora presenter in grey suit and dark tie tips his hat on a city rooftop at golden hour, medium shot, skyline behind.

regeln: Within each spoken phase use multiple distinct relevant shots, roughly 3-5 seconds each for Shorts; long videos can allow purposeful longer demonstrations. Preserve continuous narration and accurate subtitle timing.
A zoom, crop, subtitle change or decorative background does not count as a new motif. Never fill missing images with candles, unrelated stock or background-only frames.
Show the main image prominently; avoid tiny repeated photos in a mostly empty vertical frame. Preserve genuine evidence and important image details.
For AI Tools Explained identify the exact tool briefly, then show genuine interface views and different source-supported examples. Never present stock or an illustration as a real tool result.
Use original urban painted open-world-game poster styling for fictional scenes and presenters; no copied game characters. Match narrated action and era.

Clear speech and readable captions alone do not make a professional video. Inspect useful motif changes and narration-image alignment over the entire video. Missing main imagery is a substantial defect.
Include mandatory spoken like, share and save calls at the correct format-specific positions. Do not replace this requirement with a different CTA.

AI Tools Explained is for viewers with a practical task. Do not read parameter counts, architecture names, pipeline tags, context lengths or benchmark claims as a substitute for useful explanation. Explain the human task, the source-supported action and a concrete limit. A generic trending-tools question failed story review twice; prefer a specific visual workflow.

The user confirmed original presenter references on 2026-10-05: Business Origin Stories uses the blue-eyed man with a fedora, grey suit, dark tie and gold pocket watch; AI Tools Explained uses the black-haired man with black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses. Preserve identity and typical clothing, vary action and setting.

Introduce the correct presenter at the opening and bring that same presenter back during the video in useful actions. Do not confine the figure to the ending. Do not replace original channel figures with different fictional people; anonymous period workers remain clearly illustrative supporting people, never a real-founder likeness.

Prefer vivid original painted open-world-game scenes to long holds on lifeless documentary photos. Preserve factual accuracy and show authentic tool examples briefly as evidence. Camera moves alone are not new motifs or full character animation.

The user confirmed on 2026-10-05 that both new delivered videos are much better than before. Preserve the original painted world, recurring channel identity, matching main imagery, music and useful scene changes. The long-term quality target remains 10/10; the user did not give these videos a numeric score. Do not replace their actual AI scores or the existing 7/10 delivery threshold with the aspirational target.

Ensure every script features a clear narrative arc with a compelling 'why' (motivation), a dramatic turning point, and a decisive resolution.
Maintain strict narrative momentum by progressing directly from the core problem to the solution without extraneous background filler.
Integrate mandatory spoken like, share and save calls contextually into the narrative flow; do not use them as abrupt additions.
Display primary visual evidence prominently; avoid tiny repeated photos, empty backgrounds, or unrelated fillers.
Ensure all visual evidence aligns precisely with spoken data, dates, and era-appropriate source references.
Maintain continuous narration and accurate subtitle timing across all spoken phases.
Use original urban painted open-world-game poster styling for fictional scenes and presenters, ensuring they appear throughout the video, not just at the end.
Preserve original speaker identities: the blue-eyed man in fedora/suit for Business Origin Stories and the man in leather jacket/cyan glasses for AI Tools Explained.
Maintain a 60-day cool-down period for repeating specific channel topics, requiring a distinct new narrative angle if revisited.
Keep Short-form pacing distinct from long-form pacing; do not apply Short speed limits to long videos or vice-versa.

story.besserer_hook: A billion dollars was pledged to OpenAI, but only $133 million ever arrived.

kandidaten: Nine top researchers joined for less money.
The most valuable AI lab started on promises.
Researchers turned down triple their market value.
hooklabor.begruendung: Kandidat 0 ist eine prägnante, kühne Aussage ('A billion was pledged.'), die laut Datensatz die höchste Zuschauerbindung nach 3 Sekunden aufweist (31 %). Sie erzeugt sofortige Spannung und ein starkes Drama, das direkt und ehrlich durch den folgenden Satz ('Only $133 million arrived.') eingelöst wir

skript.beschreibung:
OpenAI was founded in December 2015 as a nonprofit with $1 billion pledged, but tax filings show only $133 million received by 2021. Its first researchers still joined, drawn by the mission.

belege.name: OpenAI
belege.text:
OpenAI is an American artificial intelligence (AI) public benefit corporation (PBC) headquartered in San Francisco, California. It develops "frontier" generative AI models, particularly its generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) series of large language models.
Its release of ChatGPT in November 2022 accelerated an AI boom, leading to widespread use of generative AI; as of September 2026, ChatGPT is the fifth-most-visited website globally. OpenAI also releases the GPT Image models and Codex, an AI coding agent. In March 2026, OpenAI closed a funding round with a post-money valuation of US$852 billion, making it one of the most valuable AI pure play companies in the world, rivalled only by Anthropic.
OpenAI was founded in 2015 as a nonprofit, with Elon Musk and Sam Altman as co-chairs; Musk resigned in 2018. A for-profit subsidiary was created in 2019, and a 2025 restructuring converted the subsidiary into OpenAI Group PBC, that is 26% owned by the nonprofit OpenAI Foundation. Microsoft has invested over $13 billion into OpenAI. OpenAI partners with the US government via the Stargate Project infrastructure venture, and with the Department of Defense, Los Alamos National Laboratory, and arms company Anduril Industries. Former OpenAI personnel have founded competing AI companies including Anthropic, Safe Superintelligence Inc., xAI, and Thinking Machines Lab.
OpenAI has faced multiple lawsuits for alleged deaths linked to its chatbots and copyright infringement against authors
Founding: 
In December 2015, OpenAI was founded as the nonprofit organization OpenAI, Inc., by Elon Musk, Sam Altman, Ilya Sutskever, Greg Brockman, Trevor Blackwell, Vicki Cheung, Andrej Karpathy, Durk Kingma, John Schulman, Pamela Vagata, and Wojciech Zaremba, with Musk and Altman as the co-chairs. A total of $1 billion in capital was pledged by Musk, Altman, Greg Brockman, Reid Hoffman, Jessica Livingston, Peter Thiel, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and Infosys. However, the actual capital collected significantly lagged pledges. According to tax filings, only $133 million had been received by 2021.
Musk stated in 2015 that he was partly motivated by concerns about AI safety and existential risk from artificial general intelligence. OpenAI stated that "it's hard to fathom how much human-level AI could benefit society", and that it is equally difficult to comprehend "how much it could damage society if built or used incorrectly". The startup also wrote that AI "should be an extension of individual human wills and, in the spirit of liberty, as broadly and evenly distributed as possible", and that "because of AI's surprising history, it's hard to predict when human-level AI might come within reach. When it does, it'll be important to have a leading research institution which can prioritize a good outcome for all over its own self-interest." Altman expected a decades-long project that eventually surpasses human intelligence.
In its founding charter, OpenAI defined its mission as ensuring that artificial general intelligence (AGI) "benefits all of humanity", and stated an intention to collaborate openly with other institutions by making certain patents and research publicly available, but later restricted access to its most capable models, citing competitive and safety concerns. OpenAI was initially run from Brockman's living room. In September 2016, it moved to the Pioneer Building in the Mission District, San Francisco.
Brockman met with Yoshua Bengio, one of the "founding fathers" of deep learning, and drew up a list of great AI researchers. Brockman was able to hire nine of them as the first employees in December 2015. OpenAI did not pay AI researchers salaries comparable to those of Facebook or Google. It also did not pay stock options which AI researchers typically get. Nevertheless, OpenAI spent $7 million on its first 52 employees in 2016. OpenAI's potential and mission drew these researchers to the firm; a Google employee said he was willing to leave Google for OpenAI "partly because of the very strong group of people and, to a very large extent, because of its mission." OpenAI co-founder Wojciech Zaremba stated that he turned down "borderline crazy" offers of two to three times his market value to join OpenAI instead.
In April 2016, OpenAI released a public beta of "OpenAI Gym", its platform for reinforcement learning research. Nvidia gifted its first DGX-1 supercomputer to OpenAI in August 2016 to help it train larger and more complex AI models with the capability of reducing processing time from six days to two hours. In December 2016, OpenAI released "Universe", a software platform for measuring and training an AI's general intelligence across the world's supply of games, websites, and other applications.
